lesson.menu_desc: A burst water main at Station 1 + the past passive -- 31 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 17 -- Explaining a Problem on Site
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Thiago Negrães | Lesson 17 -- Explaining a Problem on Site

listenings.text: When something goes wrong on site, the first report is usually written in a hurry, and that is where the problems start. A good incident report answers four questions. What happened? When and where was it found? What was done right after? And what is the root cause? Write it in the past, and use the passive when the person is not important: the leak was found at six, the valve was closed, the area was cleaned. Never guess the root cause in the first report. Write that it is still not confirmed, and send the full report within forty-eight hours.

Thiago, it's Dave from the site. Bad news from last night. A water main burst near Station 1 at about two in the morning. The excavation was flooded, and two of the new pumps were damaged. Nobody was hurt. The night guard called me, and the main valve was closed by the utility's team at three. This morning the water was pumped out, and the area was inspected. We think the pipe was hit by an excavator yesterday afternoon, but we need to confirm that. Call me as soon as you can.

extra_audio.text: First, a water main burst near Station 1 at two in the morning. Then, the excavation was flooded, and two pumps were damaged. After that, the main valve was closed by the utility's team. Next, the water was pumped out, and the area was inspected. Finally, the incident report was sent to the client.

items.situation: Rachel asks what happened to the excavation last night. Water filled it.
The client asks about the pumps. Two of them are broken because of the water.
tips: Add by the water: it matters here.

items.situation: Your manager wants to know if anybody was injured. Nobody was.
The client asks who closed the main valve. It was the utility's team.
tips: Start with the valve, not with the team.
Here who did it matters: use by.

items.situation: Ask Dave if the area was checked this morning.
tips: Question in the past passive: Was plus subject.
